headline.purpose: Result identity and major state headings.

title.purpose: Workflow panels and local task sections.

label.purpose: Short step and category orientation only.

shadows.name: floating-ambient
shadows.purpose: Gentle separation for menus and help surfaces that truly float above the working plane.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single high-emphasis action in a workflow region.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { min-height: 48px; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; background: rgb(var(--color-river)); color: rgb(var(--color-accent-contrast)); padding: 0 24px; font: 600 14px/20px Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: rgb(var(--color-river) / 0.9); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid rgb(var(--color-river)); outline-offset: 2px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgb(var(--color-paper)); }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A restrained bordered action for refresh, navigation, and disclosure support.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { min-height: 44px; border: 1px solid rgb(var(--color-line)); border-radius: 8px; background: rgb(var(--color-surface)); color: rgb(var(--color-river)); padding: 0 16px; font: 600 14px/20px Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: rgb(var(--color-river)); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid rgb(var(--color-river)); outline-offset: 2px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgb(var(--color-paper)); }

components.name: Panel
components.description: The standard flat, bounded region for one operational task.
components.html:
STEP 1 OF 2

Choose collateral

Select the assets to compare across borrowing paths.
components.css: .ds-panel { border: 1px solid rgb(var(--color-line)); border-radius: 12px; background: rgb(var(--color-surface)); color: rgb(var(--color-ink)); padding: 20px 24px; font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-panel h3 { margin: 4px 0 0; font-size: 20px; line-height: 28px; font-weight: 600; } .ds-panel p { margin: 8px 0 0; color: rgb(var(--color-slate)); font-size: 14px; line-height: 24px; } .ds-panel-kicker { color: rgb(var(--color-river)); font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.14em; }

components.name: Amount Field
components.description: The prominent monetary control used to compare one request across every path.
components.css: .ds-amount-field { display: block; border: 1px solid rgb(var(--color-line)); border-radius: 12px; background: rgb(var(--color-surface)); color: rgb(var(--color-ink)); padding: 16px; font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-amount-field:focus-within { border-color: rgb(var(--color-river)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgb(var(--color-river)); } .ds-amount-label { display: block; color: rgb(var(--color-slate)); font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.1em; } .ds-amount-line { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; margin-top: 8px; } .ds-amount-line input { min-width: 0; width: 100%; border: 0; outline: 0; background: transparent; color: rgb(var(--color-ink)); font: 600 30px/36px Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Workflow Steps
components.description: Two compact peer panels that preserve task orientation without becoming a full navigation system.
components.css: .ds-steps { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 8px; } .ds-step { min-height: 64px; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; border: 1px solid rgb(var(--color-line)); border-radius: 12px; background: rgb(var(--color-surface)); color: rgb(var(--color-slate)); padding: 8px 12px; } .ds-step-active { border-color: rgb(var(--color-river)); background: rgb(var(--color-info-surface)); } .ds-step-number { display: grid; width: 32px; height: 32px; place-items: center; border: 1px solid rgb(var(--color-line)); border-radius: 9999px; } .ds-step-active .ds-step-number { border-color: rgb(var(--color-river)); background: rgb(var(--color-river)); color: rgb(var(--color-accent-contrast)); }

components.name: Selection Card
components.description: A tactile asset choice that keeps balance and valuation evidence visible.
components.css: .ds-selection-card { position: relative; min-height: 128px; width: 100%; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; border: 1px solid rgb(var(--color-river)); border-radius: 12px; background: rgb(var(--color-info-surface)); color: rgb(var(--color-ink)); padding: 16px; text-align: left; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgb(var(--color-river)); } .ds-selection-check { position: absolute; top: 12px; right: 12px; display: grid; width: 24px; height: 24px; place-items: center; border-radius: 9999px; background: rgb(var(--color-river)); color: rgb(var(--color-accent-contrast)); } .ds-token { display: grid; width: 44px; height: 44px; place-items: center; border-radius: 9999px; background: rgb(var(--color-mist)); color: rgb(var(--color-river)); }

components.name: Protocol Comparison Row
components.description: The shared evidence grammar for pooled protocols and OWN.
components.css: .ds-protocol-row { overflow: hidden; border: 1px solid rgb(var(--color-line)); border-radius: 12px; background: rgb(var(--color-surface)); color: rgb(var(--color-ink)); } .ds-protocol-row button { width: 100%; border: 0; background: transparent; color: inherit; padding: 16px 20px; text-align: left; } .ds-protocol-row button:hover { background: rgb(var(--color-mist) / 0.35); } .ds-protocol-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 12px; margin-top: 16px; } .ds-protocol-grid small { display: block; color: rgb(var(--color-slate)); } .ds-protocol-grid strong { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: A compact semantic annotation, never a primary action.
components.css: .ds-status-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; border-radius: 9999px; background: rgb(var(--color-warning-surface)); color: rgb(var(--color-warning-text)); padding: 4px 10px; font: 600 12px/16px Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; }

narrative.overview:
Powerrr should feel like a private analytical instrument: calm enough to reduce financial anxiety, exact enough to earn scrutiny, and protective enough to make constraints and uncertainty visible before action. The interface favors quiet evidence over spectacle. It presents complex onchain information in a sequence of bounded, readable decisions rather than recreating the density or urgency of a trading terminal.

The visual system is restrained, tactile, and evidence-first. Limestone Paper gives the product a warm, low-noise working field; Mineral Red marks action, selection, focus, and trusted orientation. Near-black ink and warm graphite outlines bring the precision of a printed instrument docket without copying another protocol's cream-and-coral identity. Standard panels stay flat and outlined; only truly floating help or menu surfaces receive ambient lift.
keyCharacteristics: Warm mineral neutrals with one disciplined red-clay primary accent.
Clear outlined panels, gentle paper-toned grouping, and shadow only for floating surfaces.
Compact evidence grids that preserve readable labels and tabular values.
Rounded, tactile controls with visible keyboard focus and honest state language.
One deliberate light theme that remains stable regardless of system preference.

rules.name: The One Mineral Signal Rule
rules.body: Mineral Red is the only general-purpose interactive accent. Do not introduce protocol-by-protocol brand colors into the comparison hierarchy.

rules.name: The Semantic Restraint Rule
rules.body: Moss, terracotta, ochre, information blue, and warning amber carry meaning only. Never scatter them through neutral evidence for visual variety.

rules.name: The Daylight Instrument Rule
rules.body: The palette is deliberately light-only and ignores operating-system dark preference. Do not auto-invert it or quietly restore a second theme.

rules.name: The Instrument Readout Rule
rules.body: Financial values align with tabular figures and never compete with their explanatory labels through unnecessary color or weight.

rules.name: The One Display Moment Rule
rules.body: Large tight display type belongs to the pre-connect promise. Operational screens return immediately to compact task hierarchy.

rules.name: The One Decision Per Region Rule
rules.body: Each bounded region should make one task legible: choose collateral, set an amount, compare paths, or inspect evidence.

rules.name: The Stack Before Squeeze Rule
rules.body: When content no longer fits, stack or reduce columns before shrinking text, targets, or explanatory labels.

rules.name: The Border First Rule
rules.body: A border or tonal change must explain the structure before a shadow is added.

rules.name: The Ambient, Not Floating Rule
rules.body: Shadows are diffuse and low-drama. Do not use hard drop shadows, colored glows, glassmorphism, or stacked elevation for ordinary content.

rules.name: The Radius Ladder Rule
rules.body: Use 8px for controls, 12px for standard panels, and 16px only for a genuinely higher-order summary or feature region.

rules.name: The Circle Means Marker Rule
rules.body: Full circles indicate an asset, step, selection, status, or draggable point—not a generic container.

rules.name: The Equal Evidence Rule
rules.body: Comparison paths share one structural grammar even when their mechanisms differ.

rules.name: The State Plus Reason Rule
rules.body: Every unavailable, unsupported, stale, risky, or disabled state pairs a visual treatment with human-readable evidence.

dos: **Do** use Mineral Red sparingly for action, selection, progress, focus, and trusted orientation.
**Do** let Warm Graphite and Parchment Mist organize dense evidence before adding elevation.
**Do** keep operational copy direct, measured, and visibly attached to the value or state it explains.
**Do** preserve tabular figures, readable labels, and the same evidence order across responsive layouts.
**Do** maintain the single light palette as a deliberate product surface.
**Do** give OWN the same comparison structure and visual weight as pooled protocols.
donts: **Don't** introduce neon crypto palettes, protocol-brand rainbows, speculative gradients, or trading-terminal glow.
**Don't** use glassmorphism, hard shadows, floating card stacks, or decorative elevation for repeated evidence.
**Don't** turn OWN into a banner, hero, special offer, or visually dominant sales path.
**Don't** hide unsupported assets, unavailable providers, risk evidence, or explanatory labels to make the interface feel cleaner.
**Don't** shrink essential operational text below 0.75rem or interactive targets below 44px.
**Don't** use color alone to communicate availability, selection, risk, or error.
